action: Infoblox NIOS customers: expect a notice from Infoblox, review who could use saved configuration snapshots (DNS, DHCP, Grid), and rotate any secrets or credentials stored in them as a precaution.
date_note: Date Infoblox confirmed the incident to the press; the intrusion date is not stated.
exec: A network-infrastructure vendor's SharePoint data was reached through a compromised migration supplier, exposing some customer configuration data and employee personal data; counts are not published.
plain: Network software company Infoblox says someone got into some of its company files through a contractor that was moving its SharePoint data. Reports say employee and some customer configuration data were taken.
summary: An Infoblox spokesperson told The Register the company is investigating unauthorized access to certain company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor, and that it has no indication its products or cloud services were involved. The Register reports, from sources and a CEO email it saw, that some customers' NIOS configuration snapshots and employee personal data, including Social Security numbers, were taken. Counts and the vendor are not disclosed.
title: Infoblox confirms breach via third-party SharePoint migration vendor

validation.note: Company statement to the press confirms unauthorized access via a vendor; data-type details come from The Register's sources and are repeated by TechRadar and Security Affairs, so effectively single reporting origin.

review.note: Compared title, summary, date, status and single_source rating with The Register, TechRadar and Security Affairs. Infoblox statement on compromised third-party migration vendor matches.
